subject: english-language-arts
unit_title: Close Reading and Strong, Thorough Evidence
title: Launch and diagnostic: strong and thorough textual evidence
essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to strong and thorough textual evidence change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?
learning_objectives: Explain what strong and thorough textual evidence means in this unit and why it changes an interpretation or a draft.
Apply strong and thorough textual evidence to text at the level described for this course: in the grades 9-10 text complexity band, with scaffolding available at the high end of the range.
Judge the sufficiency of the learner's own evidence about strong and thorough textual evidence and revise using stated criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about strong and thorough textual evidence.
The learner gives cited textual evidence and reasoning rather than an unsupported assertion.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name the next step.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
assigned text from the course text bank, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a short retrieval prompt on strong and thorough textual evidence. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.
Name the move, show a worked example on a short passage, and make the success criteria explicit before practice begins. Keep the explanation centered on strong and thorough textual evidence.
Work two supported examples together. After each step ask, "What in the text licenses that move?" Fade prompts on the second example. The object of practice is strong and thorough textual evidence.

The learner completes a new application with the criteria checklist still available, recording the result and the reasoning that produced it. The learner writes this response; the tutor may question or critique but may not draft it.
In one concise response, state the most important claim about strong and thorough textual evidence and one check that would expose a weak or unsupported reading.

student_activity: The learner completes a new application with the criteria checklist still available, recording the result and the reasoning that produced it. Focus: strong and thorough textual evidence.
formative_check: State the most important claim about strong and thorough textual evidence and identify one check that would expose a weak or unsupported reading.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for strong and thorough textual evidence, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
Ask the learner to explain why the move for strong and thorough textual evidence works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about strong and thorough textual evidence, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of strong and thorough textual evidence.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.
Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one of them on a text the learner has not seen before.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require accurate independent application plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, at least one of them on a text the learner has not seen before.
extension: Apply the move to an unfamiliar passage of comparable complexity with the checklist available.
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and make the success criteria visible in text.
Allow typed, handwritten, dictated, or recorded-to-text responses; the response mode is not the standard.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, transcripts, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Provide an accessible reading representation (digital reflowable text, enlarged print, or audio) for every assigned text.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about writing and reading difficulty.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.
Presentation may be delivered privately to the facilitator; no public or recorded performance is ever required.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, annotated passage, recorded reading, or short clip supporting strong and thorough textual evidence.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable text, alt text, or a transcript. No media is required to meet the standard.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw drafts, raw private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one real-world instance of strong and thorough textual evidence in something they already read. No purchase, account creation, or private disclosure is required.
performance_task_link: Build an evidence-and-inference casebook on an unfamiliar text and defend two contested readings in seminar.
